The Committee was asked to consider the
proposed fees and charges as set out in Appendix A effective from
1st April 2027.
 
The annual review of charges was an important
part of the overall budget setting process and the policy framework
for service provision in general.
 
In the Spring, Officers had undertaken a
thorough review of the allotment fees and charges in preparation
for the 2027/28 fee setting cycle. 
Members of the Committee were asked to note that allotment fees
were set one year in advance, under the terms of their leases,
allotment holders must be informed of any increase in charges
twelve months before they took effect.  
 
The Committee noted that allotments were a
service widely used in the Borough with around 900 people currently
on the waiting list for an allotment.
 
 
Resolved that:
 
The proposed fees
and charges as set out in Appendix A are approved to be effective
from 1st April 2027
topline: The Environment and Sustainability Committee has decided to approve proposed fees and charges for allotments effective from 1st April 2027.

content:
The Committee received in Appendix A of the
report the proposed fees and charges for the next financial year
for the services managed by this Committee.
 
While the setting of fees and charges needed
to be considered within the overall financial context of the
Council, there would be many factors affecting their
determination.  For some charges; a full
cost recovery may be appropriate, while for others the Council may
choose to subsidise services for residents.
 
In the Spring, Officers undertook a thorough
review of their fees and charges in preparation for the 2026/27 fee
setting cycle.   The fees and
charges set out in Appendix A were based on those reviews.
 
With regards to Bowls clubs, it was noted that
it was not possible for the Council to subsidise more and sadly
some bowls clubs may have to consider merging to make them
viable.
 
It was noted that the bowls clubs in
neighbouring boroughs (Elmbridge and Spelthorne) were all
self-managed.
 
Resolved that:
 
The proposed fees
and charges as set out in Appendix A are approved to be effective
from the dates within the appendix or as soon as practical
thereafter.
topline: The Environment and Sustainability Committee has decided to approve proposed fees and charges for services, potentially impacting bowls clubs and residents.

content:
The Committee was asked to consider a report
on the current charges in the Council’s car parks, including
charges for permit and contract parking.
 
The proposed changes would be a step forward
to a fair and consistent approach to parking across the
Borough. 
 
Some members of the Committee expressed
concerns about the proposed changes, particularly in relation to
the introduction of recreational charging at additional open space
car parks.  It was noted that the sports
clubs run at the borough’s green spaces provided both a
recreational and social benefit to residents.
 
From data Officers had gathered, very few
visitors to green spaces where charging was already in place, were
parked long enough to incur a charge.  4
free parking permits for volunteers from sports groups using the
car parks were available to ensure they were not penalised.
 
 
In accordance with Standing Order 39.2 and at
the request of Cllr Saise-Marshall a named vote was taken on the
motion, and the voting was as follows: -
 
For: 6     Councillors D Whyte, Ringham,
Gahir, Gates, Milstead, S Whyte
 
Against: 3 
Councillors Kelly, Lewis, Saise-Marshall
 
 
 
Resolved that:
 
 

·               
That parking fees and permit charges should
remain unchanged for the
           
2026/27 financial year.
 

·               
The free period for Homewood Park should be
increased from 90
           
minutes to three hours to bring in line with other open space car
parks.
 
 

·               
Recreational charging should be introduced at the
additional open
           
space car parks:
 
Heathervale
Englefield Green (subject to consultation with the Crown Estate
in respect of equipment installation)
Abbeyfield
Frank
Muir Memorial Field
Ottershaw Memorial Field
Hythe
Park
 

·               
The standardisation of a two-hour 'no return
period' across all off-street
            
car parks, replacing historic individual arrangements be
approved
 

·               
The Corporate Management Committee be requested
to approve a
           
Capital estimate in the sum of £24,000 for the purchase of
new Pay and
           
Display machines for the open space car parks to be funded from
the
           
Car Parks Reserve
 
 

·               
The Corporate Management Committee be requested
to approve a
           
supplementary revenue estimate in the sum of £3,000 for the
associated
           
signage and integration to the Ring-go payments system to be
funded
           
from the Car Parks Reserve
topline: The Council has decided to approve recommendations on car park charges, including introducing recreational charging at additional open space car parks.

content:
The Committee considered a report which
outlined a proposal to release £200,000 from the Parking
Reserve fund to provide proactive maintenance in five of the
Council’s off-street car parks.
 
A recent stock condition survey had identified
a widespread state of disrepair, stemming from years of inadequate
maintenance and underinvestment.
 
The current condition of these facilities
posed a growing risk to public safety, operational efficiency, and
the long-term structural integrity of the assets. 
 
Following the stock condition survey the
Assets team had recommended an immediate investment of
£200,000 for urgent reactive maintenance across five car
parks;
 
Chertsey Library, Memorial Gardens, Woodlands,
Hummer Road and Waspe Farm.
 
The targeted spending would address the most
critical issues at each location.
 
In addition, the Committee was advised that
the Assets team would be requesting an additional £500,000
over the next five years to ensure the car parks became fully
compliant with the Environment Act 2021. 
 
Resolved that:
 
To recommend to
Corporate Management Committee the release of £200,000
from the Parking
Reserve Fund for urgent maintenance at:
 

·      
Woodlands, Chertsey

·      
Chertsey Library, Chertsey

·      
Memorial Gardens, Virginia Water

·      
Hummer Road,  Egham

·      
Waspe Farm, Egham
 
To recommend to
Corporate Management Committee the release of £5,000 for the
installation of 3 cycle racks:
 

·      
Chertsey Rec, Chertsey

·      
Chertsey Library, Chertsey

·      
Waspe Farm, Egham
 
To approve beginning
a procurement process for the services listed.
topline: The Environment and Sustainability Committee has decided to release funds for urgent maintenance in five off-street car parks and install cycle racks in three locations.

content:
Members of the Committee were asked to
consider a report on replacing ANPR for Camera Assisted Enforcement
(CAE).
 
CAE offered a modern approach to parking
management.   Upon a
vehicle’s entry to a car park, a camera captures the
car’s registration.  This
timestamped record initiated a set grace period, typically around
15 minutes, allowing the driver to pay for parking and obtain a
physical ticket.   If, after the
allocated grace period, the system detects that a ticket has not
been purchased for a specific vehicle, and an alert is sent to a
Civil Enforcement Officer (CEO).  The
CEO can then attend the car park, physically inspect the vehicles
in question, and issue a Penalty Charge Notice (PCN) where a valid
ticket is not displayed.
 
Some concerns were raised regarding the
possible implications to parking for school drop offs and
collection.    The Committee
was reminded that they had previously approved 30 minutes in
RBC’s parking orders for schools.
 
 
 
Resolved that:
 
The Committee note
the revised strategy for the Automated Number Plate Recognition
(ANPR) Project, moving from barrier-assisted to camera-assisted
enforcement (CAE).
 
The Corporate
Management Committee be asked to approve a revised capital estimate
in the sum of £110,00, down from £250,000 previously
agreed, for the camera-assisted enforcement (CAE) scheme.
topline: The Committee has decided to replace ANPR with Camera Assisted Enforcement for parking management.
